2. Gemini was slow on your chat. Your chat is 12,273 characters, which went to Gemini as one piece. I can’t tell exactly why it was slow, so I made three changes:

Faster setting. The app now asks Gemini to think less, which should speed up this kind of extraction. I couldn’t confirm the exact setting name from Google’s docs, so if Gemini rejects it, the app quietly retries without it and remembers that for the rest of the session. You can change it with GEMINI_THINKING in the .env file, or leave it empty to turn it off.

A clearer message when Gemini is too slow. It now says “Gemini did not answer within 120 seconds, twice”. Before, it said “check your internet connection”, which was misleading. It tries once more before giving up, so the longest wait is about 4 minutes, and Cancel works the whole time.

A seconds counter on the progress bar. After 8 seconds on one step it shows how long it has been, and after 40 seconds it says “Gemini is slow right now”, so a slow wait doesn’t look frozen.

I tested all of this with fake Gemini replies (56 backend checks and 45 page checks pass). If it is still slow or fails after this, send me a screenshot of the exact message. If it keeps timing out, type a faster model (one with flash-lite in its name) into the Model box.

how to run this

Here are the steps on Windows.

Close the old ChatCarry. Find the black command window from before and close it. If you can’t find it, restart the computer.

Unzip the new file. Right-click chatcarry.zip, choose Extract All, and click Extract. Open the new folder until you see app.py and start_chatcarry.bat in the same place.

Double-click start_chatcarry.bat. The first time, it sets itself up for about a minute and needs internet. A black window appears, and that is normal. Don’t close it while you use ChatCarry.

Your browser opens by itself. If it doesn’t, open Chrome and go to 127.0.0.1:5000. You should see an Import ChatGPT or Claude export button and a My projects box at the bottom, which means you have the new version.

Add your Gemini key. Paste it in the Gemini API key box on the right. To avoid pasting it every time, open the .env file in Notepad and type your key after GEMINI_API_KEY= (no spaces or quotes), save it, then close the black window and double-click start_chatcarry.bat again.

Use it. Paste your chat, or click Import ChatGPT or Claude export and choose conversations.json. Click Extract project state, check the items, then click Save project and Copy for ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini.

If the launcher doesn’t work:

If it says Python was not found, install Python from python.org and tick Add python.exe to PATH, then double-click the file again.

Or open Command Prompt in the folder (type cmd in the folder’s address bar and press Enter) and run these two lines:

  pip install -r requirements.txt

  python app.py

Then open 127.0.0.1:5000.

To stop ChatGPT-style waiting at any time, press Cancel on the page. To close the app when you are done, close the black window.

The error is “did not answer within 120 seconds, twice”, and it hit on a 22,535-character chat, almost twice the size of the one that worked. That points to Gemini taking too long on big chunks. I suspect one cause I can fix: I’m asking Gemini to copy all the code in your chat back out, word for word, which is slow and could even change the code. I’ll look at that part of the app.

I changed ChatCarry to make big chats faster and sent you a new chatcarry.zip. I could not test it with real Gemini, because I don’t have a key here. My own tests pass, but the speed fix is not proven yet.

Do this now, before the new version: in the Model box, type gemini-3.5-flash-lite and extract again. If that name is rejected, check Google AI Studio for the current model names. Flash-lite models are the fastest.

Why it was slow: your chat has a lot of code. I was asking Gemini to write all that code back word for word. That is a huge answer, so it took more than 120 seconds. Your first chat was smaller, so it worked.

What I changed in v2.2:

Code no longer goes through Gemini. The app copies the code straight from your chat, so it is always exact. Gemini only reads the first 12 lines of each code block and says if it worked, failed or was not tested. This is the main fix.

Smaller parts. Chats are cut into parts of 10,000 characters instead of 14,000, so each wait is shorter.

A “Test Gemini speed” button in Settings. Press it first. If that tiny question is also slow, the problem is the model or your internet, not your chat.

A better timeout message. It now says which part failed and which model you used, for example “Part 3 of 5, 9,800 characters, model gemini-3.8-flash”.

Tests: 63 backend tests, 9 importer tests and 75 browser tests all pass. The app tests used fake Gemini answers.

To use it:

Close the old ChatCarry window.

Unzip the new file into a fresh folder.

Run start_chatcarry.bat.

Press Test Gemini speed in Settings.

Extract your 22,535-character chat again.

If it still times out, send me the new error message, which now names the part and the model.

give me the summary of this whole chat

Summary of our whole chat

Your problem: When an AI chat gets too long, it hits a limit. You cannot continue it, and copying it into another AI loses the decisions, the code and the bugs.

What we found: Tools for this already exist, such as ContextBridge, SessionBridge and MemoryPlugin. You did not want to copy them. This is a portfolio project, so we chose a different angle.

What we built: ChatCarry. It does not just copy the chat. It makes a project state that you can check:

Paste or import a chat. You can paste text, upload a file, or import a ChatGPT or Claude export.

Extract with Gemini: goal, tech stack, requirements, decisions, completed work, bugs, “do not change” rules, next tasks and the latest code.

Review and edit. Every item links back to the message it came from.

Copy a handoff to paste into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini.

Save the project. Later you can add a new chat and it merges into the same project.

What makes it different:

source links for every item

replaced decisions are marked (“use SQLite instead of Firebase”)

conflicting decisions are flagged

only the newest version of each file is kept

numbers like 120 and 130 are never merged

secrets such as API keys are removed before anything is sent

Technology: Python and Flask, a one-page HTML and JavaScript interface, the Gemini API, and saved projects as JSON files. It has 63 backend tests, 9 importer tests and browser tests.

How it went:

You ran it and Gemini worked on your StoryDNA chat. We checked the output and most items were correct.

You hit errors along the way. One was an old copy still running, and another was a missing file.

The latest error was a 120-second timeout on a long chat (22,535 characters).

I made v2.2: the app now copies code itself instead of asking Gemini, parts are smaller, and there is a “Test Gemini speed” button.

Not tested yet:

The v2.2 fix with real Gemini.

The Windows launcher.

Real ChatGPT and Claude export files.

Your next steps:

Run v2.2 and extract the long chat again. If it still times out, use a flash-lite model.

Test 3–4 of your own chats and count how many extracted items are correct.

Record a short demo video and take screenshots.

Put it on GitHub with the README.

Write a 150-word portfolio description.

I can write the demo script or the portfolio description for you if you want.
